name: Dental Ankylosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Dental Ankylosis

criteria.description: Absence of physiological tooth mobility on clinical examination
High-pitched, metallic percussion sound on tapping the affected tooth
Radiographic evidence of loss of periodontal ligament space and fusion of tooth root to alveolar bone
Clinical infraocclusion or submergence of the affected tooth relative to adjacent teeth
Lack of exfoliation of primary teeth due to ankylosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical immobility, high-pitched percussion tone, and radiographic evidence of ankylosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by radiographic findings; differential diagnosis includes other causes of infraocclusion.

imaging: Loss of periodontal ligament space on radiographs
Direct fusion of tooth root to alveolar bone on panoramic or periapical X-rays
Infraocclusion visible on clinical and radiographic examination
genetic: Possible familial predisposition reported but no definitive genetic markers identified
other: Clinical percussion test producing metallic sound
Lack of physiological tooth mobility on clinical exam

distinguishingFeatures: Primary tooth retention lacks radiographic fusion
Radiographic evidence of root surface irregularity
No ankylosis or fusion to bone

redFlags: Progressive ankylosis leading to facial asymmetry
Failure of exfoliation causing malocclusion and impaction
references: Andreasen JO, et al. Dental ankylosis: clinical and radiographic features. Int J Oral Sci. 2018.
Neville BW, et al. Oral & Maxillofacial Pathology, 4th Edition. 2015.
